forecaster_note: As the weekend's coastal low moves away we're left with a nice-sized short-period mix of S and E/NE swell for peaky, head-high surf. Light SW winds through the morning for the cleanest conditions, onshores kicking in later for bump and chop. Tue: easing ENE + S, waist to chest, clean in the morning. Wed–Thu: windy onshore south swell — a skip unless the wind swings SW. — Surfline forecaster (Mon 5 Oct)

wind.summary: Light SW 7 kph offshore at 6am, near-calm at 9am, then E onshore 9 kph by noon building to ~15 kph by 3pm.

shark.summary: Northern Beaches, last 24h: one SLS drone shark sighting at Whale Beach (7:33am Sun, ~22h ago). Nothing at Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl or Manly. Feed current (newest statewide activity <1h old; 40+ detections statewide, mostly Central/South Coast and Mid-North Coast). Check the live map before paddling out.

days.label: Today
days.note: Peaky NE 5.6ft @ 10s (~700 kJ) plus short S — chest to head, light SW then calm 6–9am. Best window 6–10am; Dee Why and Manly rate fair-good early. Onshore E kicks in by noon, ~15 kph by 3pm. High 4:36am, low 10:03am — dropping tide through the morning.

swells.label: Dominant NE swell — the good angle, a notch longer period than yesterday
Short-period S swell (dead-S angle — wraps poorly at Dee Why, fine at the exposed magnets)

dee-why.window: SW 7 kph offshore at 6am, glassy by 9am, E onshore by noon. Falling tide to the 10:03am low. NE 58° is the right angle; the S component wraps poorly here.

tip.label: Frontside rights at the Point
tip.text: Punchy NE — take the Point on your forehand, backside lefts on the beach peaks. 10s gives a bit more push than yesterday; sit a touch wider on the outside.

long-reef.window: Cross-shore light SW early, calm ~9am then onshore E from noon. Picks up the most size and the S wedge. Low tide 10:03am will hollow the banks.

tip.label: Frontside rights off the reef
tip.text: Biggest of the four — sit deep on the peak, commit on the drop and use the wedgey sections on your forehand.

curl-curl.window: Light SW cross-shore to 9am, glassy-ish at the 10am low. Peaky banks; north end cleanest once the E breeze comes up.

tip.label: Find the bank
tip.text: Peaky with a S wedge in the mix — find the bank holding shape and take the shoulder.

manly.window: Light SW offshore at 6am, calm 9am. Falling tide to the 10am low. Sheltered corner handles the S component better than Dee Why.

tip.label: Backside lefts, frontside rights
tip.text: Peaks both ways — go left on the backhand off the S wedge, rights off the NE energy.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Easing ENE + S mix, waist to chest high. Clean offshore W 8–11 kph through the morning, light onshores in the arvo. Aim for the lower tide (low 11:19am; high 5:42am).

dee-why.window: Offshore W ~9–11 kph all morning, onshore by arvo. Slightly smaller than Mon — aim for the low around 11am.

long-reef.window: Rates best of the four early (fair-good 3–9am). Offshore W through the morning.

curl-curl.window: Fair-good at first light, offshore W, easing as the swell drops.

manly.window: Clean with W offshore through the morning; fun and mellow.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Early look (low confidence): Wed–Thu big onshore S swell, a skip. Winds go more favourable end of week, cleaning up the easing S/SE swell — Surfline flags Fri/Sat as the window. Check back Friday.
